coverage.evidence: The 30 rows match the page's table and its '30 template helpers' description. EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:20-56 sets the argument counts: emote takes 1-2, image and provider take 1, repeat takes 2 and wall takes 3. EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:115-121 gives cheermote 1 argument. EmoteSetHelpers.cs:17-28 and 34-43 build list, count and the 7tv/bttv/ffz set rows, and EmoteRandomHelpers.cs:17-49 builds random, sub, follower, bits, global and any. EmoteUsageHelpers.cs:20-29, EmoteFavoriteHelpers.cs:17-22 and EmoteMessageHelpers.cs:17-32 build the rest. EmoteRow.cs:65 (Over) gives the pick, list and count rows 0 to 0 arguments, so they take none.

EmoteRow.cs:87-90 returns null on a wrong argument count, and ITemplateHelperProvider.cs:42 plus TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:46 render a null token as written. EmoteRandomHelpers.cs:53-54 returns empty for an empty pick. EmoteText.cs:24-25 joins a list one space apart, and EmoteText.cs:27-28 formats a count with N0 in the channel culture (EmoteRow.cs:27), so 0 prints as '0' and 1204 as '1,204' in English. EmoteItem.cs:42-49 maps providers to 7TV, BTTV, FFZ and Twitch. EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:127-145 picks the Cheer prefix and the biggest tier whose MinBits is at or below the amount, returns empty when no tier fits, and returns null for a non-whole amount or one below 1.

TemplateHelperContexts.cs:21-22: Standard is Command, EventResponse, Timer, Pipeline, Discord and Webhook (TemplateHelperContext.cs:18-63). TemplateHelperContexts.cs:32-45: WithTriggerViewerAndDiscord leaves out Timer. EmoteRow.cs:77-85 makes Standard the default and switches ForViewer rows to WithTriggerViewerAndDiscord. The four ForViewer rows are user.top, user.top.count, message.count and message.first (EmoteUsageHelpers.cs:22-29, EmoteMessageHelpers.cs:24,32), which matches the Use in column.

EmoteText.cs:31-38 tries an exact ordinal match first, then a case-insensitive one. EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:62-66 returns the code, else the fallback after the pipe, else empty. EmoteText.cs:19-21 sets MaxRepeat 50, MaxWallRows 10 and MaxWallColumns 20. EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:93-94 reads argument 1 as rows and argument 2 as columns, and line 59 sets the row break to ' / '. EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:108-109 with ParsedArgument.cs:27-28 accepts digits only within 1..max and returns null for anything else, so the token stays as written. An unknown emote gives empty (EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:72,85).

EmoteSetHelpers.cs:78-79 filters with IsChannelSetOf, which is the origin plus InChannel (EmoteItem.cs:51), so a network set holds that channel set only and no globals. EmoteData.cs:198-211 says the third-party sources include channel sets and globals. EmoteRandomHelpers.cs:17-35 filters by subscriptions, follower and bitstier (EmoteItem.cs:37-39). EmoteRandomHelpers.cs:36-49 has global read GlobalAsync and any read AllAsync. EmoteRow.cs:30-34 picks with Random.Shared on each render (EmoteTemplateHelpers.cs:32). An empty pool gives empty for pick and list and '0' for count.

EmoteData.cs:46 sets UsageWindow to 5000. DbEmoteChatSource.cs:31-33 drops IsCommand lines and takes the newest 5000. EmoteText.cs:69-75 breaks a tie with an ordinal ThenBy, so 'K' (75) sorts before 'c' (99). EmoteUsageHelpers.cs:49 returns empty when nothing was used. EmoteUsageHelpers.cs:56-60 gives an empty stream filter when CurrentStreamId is null, and ChannelOfflineHandler.cs:145 nulls it when the stream goes offline. EmoteUsageHelpers.cs:61-65 filters the viewer by platform id. EmoteFavoriteHelpers.cs:21 takes the first favorite, and FavoriteEmoteService ListAsync orders by CreatedAt descending for the channel owner (DbEmoteChatSource.cs:38-49), so it gives the most recently starred emote. In dashboard EmotePicker.vue:330-336 a right-click toggles the star, and chat i18n en.json:292 labels the picker 'Emotes and emoji'.

EmoteRow.cs:95 adds the Viewer context only when ViewerText is set, and only emote.repeat sets it (EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:44-48). EmoteLookupHelpers.cs:80-85 returns null in viewer text for a code that is not plain, and EmoteText.cs:41-49 rejects whitespace, < > { }, www. and absolute URLs, so the viewer's token stays as written. The same lines return null for an unknown emote. EmoteTemplateHelpers.cs:87 skips argument rendering in viewer text, so nested helpers are not run. The ForViewer rows leave out Timer, and features.mdx:51 names the Viewer Templates setting and its permission.

reader_answers.evidence: The set table rows and the sub, follower, bits, global and any picks exist as named (EmoteSetHelpers.cs:17-43, EmoteRandomHelpers.cs:17-49). Over rows take 0 arguments (EmoteRow.cs:65).

The catalogue is the channel emotes, the Twitch globals and the third-party channel sets with their globals (EmoteData.cs:123-132, 198-211). Viewer and message rows leave out Timer (TemplateHelperContexts.cs:32-45, EmoteRow.cs:80-85).

A pick uses Random.Shared on each render (EmoteRow.cs:30-34). A list is space-joined (EmoteText.cs:24-25), and a count uses N0 in the channel culture (EmoteText.cs:28). The network sets hold the channel set only (EmoteSetHelpers.cs:79, EmoteItem.cs:51). The usage helpers count stored chat lines (DbEmoteChatSource.cs:21-35), while the favorite reads the owner's stars (EmoteData.cs:234-249).

PickCode returns empty for an empty pool (EmoteRandomHelpers.cs:53-54). An extra argument makes RenderAsync return null, so the token is rendered as written (EmoteRow.cs:87-90, TemplateTreeRenderer.cs:46). Count gives N0 of 0, which is '0' (EmoteText.cs:28).
